sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Éber, also spelt Eber or Ébir, ranks as an Irish hero. Several characters in the Book of Invasions carry the name. Some say it derives from Eber, or Heber, in the Book of Genesis. The chief was Éber Finn, leader of the Milesians. He was the son of Míl Despaine, known as Mil of Spain and the Spanish soldier. After the Milesians beat the Tuatha Dé Danann, Éber Finn took the south of Ireland. His brother Éremón was granted the north. Éber Finn thought his share smaller than that of his brother. He started a war he could not win, and he died in it. Éber Donn was the envious older brother of Éber Finn. He filled a small place in Irish myth. Writers often merged him with Donn, the king of death. One can easily mistake one Éber for the other. They may once have been a single figure.

key_results: Éber is a name shared by several figures in the Book of Invasions.
Éber Finn was chief of the Milesians and took the south of Ireland.
Éber Finn died after a failed war against his brother Éremón.
Éber Donn was often confused with Donn, the king of death.
